complaint: Honestly the logs are unusable. I scroll for a minute and it's all health checks.

response.restated_complaint: The engineer is complaining that logs are dominated by noise (health checks and similar) making it hard to find useful message-related entries.

hypotheses.summary: 95.7% of all log records (2700 of 2820) carry no correlation_id or trace_id and can't be joined to any message. Of those, health_check lines alone account for 42.6% of total volume (1200 records), queue_depth_gauge another 42.6%, and poll_chatter 10.6%. Only 120 lines (4.3%) are actually message-scoped and useful for debugging — this matches the complaint of scrolling through mostly health-check noise.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Directly quantifies the 'all health checks' complaint and shows health_check logging is the single largest noise source.

hypotheses.summary: The queue_depth gauge log line is emitted 1200 times (contributing 42.6% of total log volume) but every record has the same value (0), no attributes, and no trace_id — it measures nothing useful while adding as much volume to the logs as the health checks do. This is a second, distinct source of the noise the engineer is scrolling through.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Separate finding_id from the log_noise finding, showing a second concrete driver of log volume bloat (not just health checks) with equal contribution to the noise problem.

would_resolve: Whether health_check and queue_depth_gauge emission can be suppressed or routed to a separate low-priority stream
Confirmation from the engineering team on which log line patterns should be filtered by default in the log viewer
